title.label: Two Years of Training Data. Still Doing the Programming Myself.

content.label:
I’ve been subscribed to Fitbod since 2024, yet I still do virtually all the workout programming myself. Despite extensive training history, exercise substitutions, preferences, and corrections, I routinely rebuild its recommendations rather than follow them.

The Beta Coach mostly points out the obvious like identifying the element of an upcoming workout instead of delivering actionable insights. Progress reports emphasize activity totals while overlooking meaningful strength progression and exercise-specific personal records. 

I continue subscribing primarily for strength scores and my workout history data (baselines/ records), not personalized programming. These tracking features alone hardly justify premium pricing when the app’s core functionality still requires extensive manual intervention.

Fitbod claims its AI learns from training and workout adjustments to deliver personalized programming. After more than two year of providing both, why am I still doing virtually all the programming myself and what actually justifies $96 annually?

title.label: Good, but improvements can definitely be made.

content.label:
Overall, I like this app and have used it for years. It will put together workouts for you, let you create your own, focus on splits, etc. It’s good to track workouts and progress over time.

My biggest complaint is that it does not suggest very good weights to use a lot of the time. For example, in my last workout, it calculated I should use 7.5 pound weights for a specific exercise, when the last time I did it, I used 40 pound weights. The app said it was because it had been so long since I had done that exercise. It had been three months and I did similar exercises in the meantime. 

Or it won’t update weights. It continues to suggest the same weight for squats, going on ten weeks now. Great that it plans workouts, but far less useful when it does things like that. And it doesn’t always go too light - do three sets of 8 pull-ups, now the app says you can do 13 reps.

And it seems to get stuck in a loop with the weights. I have dumbbells that go in 2.5 pound increments, but 95%of the time, the app only suggests 27.5 pounds, 32.5, 37.5, etc. I have no idea why it acts like it’s allergic to 25, 30, 35, but its suggestions and calculations take away the benefit of being able to slowly increase weight by 2.5 pounds. That’s just more of an annoyance than a problem with the app, but it still impacts how it plans workouts, limiting the usefulness.

title.label: Good app, great for any level of training

content.label:
I’ve had this app for almost 5 years. I think that says enough, but I’ll continue. I love the versatility of the app, by that I mean there are multiple “automatic” settings that you can set if you want the app to build workouts for you, help you figure out how many exercises you should be doing and more. I generally use it more to help my build my own workouts and keep track of what I like. It helps track your goals and progress as well. There are some things I’d change but that can be said for basically every app in existence.

For the devs: my only recent thought would be that it’d be awesome if there was a calendar tab in the app. To see what workouts were upcoming and more. For me I like building weeks ahead what workouts I’m going to do and I’m sure other people would feel the same. That way if people only like runs or bikes on certain days, instead of having to change the exercise everytime the app says to do it. They can plan ahead what workouts for what days and what exercises they’re going to do. I’m sure it would help people stay on track and look ahead at what the app has in store for them. It would also help a great way to track progress and see future benchmarks. Also a way to write notes on the app, for different exercises and such.
